questions.q: Propyne reacts with water in the presence of HgSO₄ and dilute H₂SO₄. The product is:
questions.explain: Water adds in the Markovnikov sense to give the enol CH₃–C(OH)=CH₂, which tautomerises to acetone. Propanal is the anti-Markovnikov (hydroboration) product.

questions.q: Which alkyne gives an aldehyde on hydration with HgSO₄/dil. H₂SO₄?
questions.explain: Only ethyne (acetylene) gives an aldehyde, acetaldehyde. Every other alkyne gives a ketone; terminal alkynes give methyl ketones.

questions.q: Pent-2-yne is hydrated using HgSO₄ in dilute H₂SO₄. The product is:
options: A mixture of pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one
questions.explain: The two carbons of this unsymmetrical internal triple bond are similarly substituted, so water adds at either one and a mixture of two ketones forms. A symmetrical alkyne such as but-2-yne gives a single ketone.

questions.q: To convert propyne into propanal instead of acetone, the reagent to choose is:
options: Hg²⁺ and H⁺ at higher temperature
questions.explain: Hydroboration–oxidation adds water anti-Markovnikov and gives the aldehyde. All the mercury/acid conditions are Kucherov conditions and give the methyl ketone.
